Text.Text: The preserve sounds easier these days. Keep listening to your beast. When you're ready to work on Alpha Rhythm, come find me; I can hear the difference already.
You keep asking your beast to follow before you've listened. Bring your Beast Mastery to rank 50, then return. We can work on the lead after that.

Listen past the trees. The handlers in the Tarn Jungle Preserve are forcing their beasts into the same killing rhythm. Six Alpha Rhythm adepts started it. Defeat those six and bring me their hunt tally. I want to know which packs they've put through this.
Take the key to the preserve entrance in the Tarnished Jungles. Listen before you move. Your beast may hear the trouble before you do.

A forced lead sets a rhythm the whole line has to follow whether it wants to or not. Adepts goad a beast into that position instead of letting one earn it. Sounds close to a real pack rhythm if you don't know better. It isn't. It's just noise wearing a beat's shape.
A true lead doesn't force tempo. It offers one, and the pack chooses to follow because the choice keeps everyone alive together. That's rhythm. Command without choice is just noise with good timing.

Every true count this preserve ever kept got scratched onto that tally, generation over generation. Adepts use it to fake a rhythm they never earned. Bring it back and the true count's mine to read again, not theirs to counterfeit.
Six Alpha Rhythm adepts in the Tarn Jungle Preserve. Bring their hunt tally here to the Waterfall Ruins when you've stopped them.
You're moving different. Steadier. Let me see what you brought back.
There's the true count, home again. Preserve's already sitting a little straighter for it. More noise further in, if you want to keep quieting it.

Five specialists are keeping that rhythm going with scent. No pack gets to choose when to rest. Beat the five in the preserve and bring me their scent vial. I want to know what's being forced into the air.
Go back to the preserve. Listen for your beast before you answer anything they've put in the air.

Dosed to force a tempo through scent alone, no choosing involved anywhere in it. Bring that vial back and I've got the forced beat isolated, proof of exactly how they've been playing this preserve like an instrument that never agreed to be played.

Earning a beat takes patience. Forcing one takes a vial and no conscience. They chose the vial because it's faster, and because a pack that's forced doesn't ask questions about who's leading it. Efficient. Also completely dishonest.

A frightened pack can move at the same time without trusting its lead. You'll hear the difference when one beast misses a step: the handlers punish it instead of helping the pack settle. A rhythm freely followed can survive that stumble.
Five specialists are dosing the preserve's packs. Deal with them and bring me the scent vial.
You've got the rhythm of it now, I think. Let's hear what you brought.
Forced beat, isolated and dead. That's proof this preserve can use. You're keeping better time every visit.

The warden carries the preserve's alpha totem. He's the one the handlers make their beasts follow. Call him out at the preserve's challenge marker, defeat him, and bring me that totem. Take others along; give the pack more than one voice to answer.
Call the warden at the preserve's challenge marker. Listen to anyone you've brought as much as you listen to him. Your beast still has a rhythm of its own.

Fast, relentless, alone. He set that tempo himself once, honestly, before the crew got their hands on him and taught him to force it onto anyone standing near. Half the man I remember is still in that beat somewhere. The other half is exactly why you need company.

Alpha totem marks the true lead of a pack line, the one every follower chose freely. He's carrying it clawed apart because he stopped being a true lead the day he started forcing his beat instead of earning it. Bring it back whole and the true lead is honored again.

A fast rhythm can sweep you into reacting before you notice it. Other hunters give you something familiar to listen for while you catch your breath. Choose people who can hear each other under pressure.
The preserve's challenge marker calls the warden. Beat him and bring the alpha totem to me.
Your whole pack still moving. Good rhythm holds. Let me see the totem.
Whole. The true lead's honored again, first time in longer than this preserve's kept count. Rest your pack. The ones who taught him that beat are next, and they know it's coming.
Four keepers made the forced rhythm into doctrine. They still hold the keeper's token in the preserve. Defeat all four and bring it back. A pack deserves a lead it can leave.
Four keepers, all trying to make you follow them. Keep listening to your own pack first.

Force instead of earn, drum instead of offer, and they wrote it all down and taught it like scripture to anyone who'd listen. A pack built on that never actually moves together. It just moves at the same time, right up until it doesn't, and then it's four soloists standing where a pack used to be.

That token's the true count of who's allowed to call tempo for this whole preserve. They minted false copies to cover for each other. One real token in my hands, and every false beat they've called since gets silenced with it.

Listen to each other before you answer the keepers. If you've brought hunters, agree who watches which approach. If it's you and your beast, leave room to hear what it notices. The keepers would rather you rushed.
Four keepers still hold the token in the preserve. Bring it home when you've broken their circle.
Whole pack, still together. Let's hear what you brought.
Whole. Their false beat's silenced for good. One rhythm left down there, and it's the one every other broken beat in this preserve got copied from. Your pack's ready for that one, I think.

The master sets the rhythm for every handler you fought. He's in the Alpha Beast Hollow now. Use its challenge marker to call him, and beat him before another pack is taught to follow by fear. Come back afterward. I want to hear how your beast moved.
The Alpha Beast Hollow has the master's challenge marker. Take your own rhythm in with you. He's used to everyone listening only to his.

Because it's not a lie built from nothing. It's the true rhythm, the one I've spent my life teaching, bent just enough that it still sounds honest while it forces everyone near it to follow. You've been learning to offer a beat and let a pack choose it freely. He learned the same beat and decided choosing was optional. That's the whole difference, and it's the whole danger.
Listen for your own pack. If you go alone, watch your beast instead of watching only him. His rhythm becomes harder to resist when you forget there was another one before it.

Goes back to true tempo, offered and chosen, the way a pack's supposed to move. I'll be listening for it every day after this, and the day it sounds honest again all the way through, I'll know you finished the job right.
Call the master in the Alpha Beast Hollow. Once he's beaten, return to the Waterfall Ruins. I'll listen here.
Quiet. Whole preserve's gone quiet, no beat at all, first time in longer than I've been listening. Tell me it's him.
Hear that? The pack isn't being driven anymore. Keep listening to your own beast in the same way. If you still want to learn Alpha Rhythm, we have a much better place to begin now.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the six and bring the tally.
What do you mean, a wrong beat?
How does a lead beast set tempo for a pack?
What's this tally to your rhythm?
Let me listen a while longer.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Tarn Hunt Tally.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the five and bring the vial.
What's the vial doing to the tempo?
Why force a beat instead of earning one?
Can a pack even move honestly under a forced tempo?
Give me a little more time.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Beast-Pen Scent Vial.
Back to the beat.
I'll answer his beat with my own.
What's his rhythm like, exactly?
What does the alpha totem mean in your rhythm-language?
Why bring other hunters?
My pack isn't gathered yet.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Clawed Alpha Totem, whole.
Back to the beat.
We'll answer all four beats together.
What did they turn into doctrine?
What does the keeper's token mean to your rhythm?
How do we keep our own rhythm?
My pack needs rest first.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Preserve Keeper's Token, whole.
Back to the beat.
Our whole pack, answering his beat together.
What makes his rhythm so seductive?
How do I resist his rhythm?
What happens to the preserve's rhythm, once he's gone?
Let me make sure everyone is ready.
It's done. His beat broke.
